name: Battle of Königgrätz

phases.title: The armies take position either side of the river
phases.text: The Prussians took their position west of the Bystřice river. The Austrian infantry stood partly fortified, with artillery behind it and cavalry in the rear, and the Saxons on the Austrian left.

phases.title: Austrian guns pin down the Prussian right
phases.text: The Austrian artillery opened fire on the Prussian right under Herwarth von Bittenfeld. The Saxons fell back in good order and fired on the advancing Prussians from higher ground. Around 10 am the advance guard of seven battalions was pulled back to the river.

phases.title: The 7th Division advances into the Swiepwald
phases.text: The Prussian centre under Fransecky led the advance into the Swiepwald, where two Austrian corps met it. The division had to clear the forest and cover the Prussian left until the Second Army arrived.

phases.title: The First Army crosses and Sadová is taken
phases.text: King Wilhelm I ordered the First Army across the river to support Fransecky. Sadová was captured, but a fierce battle followed in a nearby forest.

phases.title: Austrian artillery halts the Prussian attack
phases.text: The Austrian artillery fired into the smoke of the Prussian advance. The advancing Prussian 8th and 4th Divisions were cut down as soon as they came out of it, and the attack was halted.

phases.title: Pöckh's charge drives the 7th Division back
phases.text: The Austrian centre began a manoeuvre to flank the 7th Division. Colonel Pöckh was sent to drive the Prussians back, and with a fierce infantry charge forced the division back to the outskirts of the forest.

phases.title: Flanking fire destroys Pöckh's battalion
phases.text: Fire from the 8th Division raked Pöckh's battalion, ended it as a fighting force and killed its commander. The 8th Division stiffened the Prussian centre against the Austrian thrusts.

phases.title: The Second Army reaches the field
phases.text: Crown Prince Frederick William arrived with the main bulk of the Second Army and hit the Austrian right flank as it retired from the Swiepwald. The 1st Guard came with it.

phases.title: The 1st Guard reaches the Austrian artillery
phases.text: Hiller von Gaertringen's 1st Guard reached the Austrian artillery, which had been trying to form a line again. It destroyed the one cavalry battery that stayed to fight and forced the other guns to flee.

phases.title: The Second Army breaks through and takes Chlum
phases.text: The Second Army completely broke through the Austrian lines and took Chlum behind the centre, as the Austrian centre was rolled up.

phases.title: The Army of the Elbe breaks the Austrian left
phases.text: The Army of the Elbe, which had merely held position since the morning, attacked and broke through the Austrian left flank. It seized Probluz and went on to destroy the flank.

phases.title: Austrian cavalry cover the retreat
phases.text: Benedek ordered a general retreat and a series of cavalry countercharges to back up his artillery and cover it. The cavalry kept the bridges over the Elbe open, at a cost of 2,000 men and almost as many horses.

note: The accounts put the Prussians west of the Bystřice river, the Saxons on the Austrian left, the 7th Division in the Prussian centre and Chlum behind the Austrian centre; they do not give compass directions or exact positions, so the plan is schematic. Which Prussian formation stood left or right of the others, and where the Austrian right stood before the Second Army came, is placed by judgement. The Second Army is drawn arriving on the Austrian right, as the accounts say it struck that flank.
